It also specifies two amplifying conditions: cognitive coupling and accountability-defensibility. These conditions raise the operational and justificatory costs of deviating from algorithmic baselines. The erosion of operational contestability unfolds through a recurrent process of Encoding, Habituation, and Closure (EHC): representations and authority rules are built into system design, algorithmic outputs become planning baselines, and those baselines become operational commitments under time pressure, interdependence, and accountability exposure. Generative AI intensifies this process by turning recommendations, explanations, and justifications into portable decision artifacts, thereby accelerating habituation and making closure less visible. The framework reframes human-AI collaboration as an operations management problem: governing decision systems so that representation, authority, and learning remain contestable across repeated decision cycles.
palavras_chave: human-AI collaboration; operational contestability; AI-enabled operations; decision-system governance; generative AI

titulo: Automatic Product Classification in International Trade: Machine Learning and Large Language Models
autores: de Artinano, IM; Depetris, FR; Martincus, CV
resumo: Accurate product classification is crucial in international trade. In this study, we apply and assess several algorithms to automatically classify agricultural and food products based on text descriptions sourced from different public agencies, including customs authorities and the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). We find that while traditional machine learning (ML) models tend to perform well within the dataset on which they are trained, their precision drops dramatically when applied to external datasets. In contrast, large language models (LLMs) show a consistently strong performance across all datasets. The top performing LLMs-Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4-achieve accuracy rates of approximately 80% at classifying products into 6-digit Harmonized System (HS) categories and above 90% for HS 2-digit Chapters. Our analysis highlights the valuable role that artificial intelligence can play in facilitating product classification at scale and, more generally, in enhancing the categorization of unstructured data.
palavras_chave: large language models; machine learning; product classification; trade

titulo: Expertise and Information Seeking in the Age of Generative AI: New Procedures, New Problematics
autores: Lodoen, S; Orchard, A
veiculo: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON TECHNOLOGY AND SOCIETY
resumo: As generative AI chatbots reroute procedures around information seeking, challenges increase with assessing and implementing relevant source material. Interactions between users and chatbots differ from prior paradigms of information seeking such as retrieval and archival systems (search engines, library catalogs, and physical stacks). AI chatbots summarize information probabilistically through dialogic interactions, leveraging natural language signifiers of expertise and intelligence to influence users' perception of their trustworthiness. This new mode of information seeking could present significant risks for users who engage with AI chatbots without clear expectations or expertise on the topic of their query. At this juncture, it is important to develop an understanding of how the procedures surrounding information-seeking practices are informed by users' values, experiences, and expectations-and how this might in future be altered by the emerging turn towards AI "experts" and authority. Our methodology in this paper comes from Ian Bogost's concept of procedural rhetoric, which examines how arguments are constructed (and persuasion takes place) through rule-based processes. We investigate how interactions relating to high-stakes domains that value accuracy and precision, such as medicine and academic research, are subtly (and not-so-subtly) reshaping users' experiences and expectations surrounding information seeking.
palavras_chave: Artificial intelligence; Modeling; Chatbots; Generative AI; Occupational health; Medical services; Technology; Search engines; Rhetoric; Context; Generative artificial intelligence; information seeking; procedural rhetoric; chatbots; expertise; research

titulo: When Your Boss Is an AI Bot: Exploring Opportunities and Risks of Manager Clone Agents in the Future Workplace
autores: Hu, Q; Xiao, Q; Cao, HC; Shen, H
veiculo: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 2026 CHI CONFERENCE ON HUMAN FACTORS IN COMPUTING SYSTEMS, CHI 2026
resumo: As Generative AI (GenAI) becomes increasingly embedded in the workplace, managers are beginning to create Manager CloneAgents-AI-powered digital surrogates trained on their work communications and decision patterns to perform managerial tasks on their behalf. To investigate this emerging phenomenon, we conducted six design fiction workshops (n = 23) with managers and workers, in which participants co-created speculative scenarios and discussed how Manager Clone Agents might transform collaborative work. We identified four potential roles that participants envisioned for Manager Clone Agents: proxy presence, informational conveyor, productivity engine, and leadership amplifier, while highlighting concerns spanning individual, interpersonal, and organizational levels. We provide design recommendations envisioned by both parties for integrating Manager Clone Agents responsibly into the future workplace, emphasizing the need to prioritize workers' perspectives and nurture interpersonal bonds while also anticipating alternative futures that may disrupt managerial hierarchies.
palavras_chave: Manager Clone Agents; AI Agent; Future of Work; Generative AI; Future Workplace; Human-AI Collaboration

titulo: Bounded Delegation: How Student Design Teams Keep Strategic Control over Generative AI
autores: Wei, BZ; Qiao, Y
resumo: Generative AI is increasingly embedded in team-based design, yet little is known about how teams negotiate its role over extended projects. We conducted a four-week situated study with nine graduate design teams (54 students) developing complete murder mystery Live Action Role-Playing games. Using domestication theory as a sensitizing framework, we analyzed 104 human-AI collaboration events, project outputs, and 27 semi-structured interviews. We identified three collaboration modes: Task-Based Empowered Creation, AI-Augmented Creative Co-creation, and Progressive Trust-Informed Collaboration. A fourth mode, Ceding Executive Trust Collaboration, was theoretically possible but did not occur. Across teams, AI was delegated tactical tasks such as content and asset generation, while humans retained control over narrative direction, quality standards, and core mechanics. We conceptualize this pattern as bounded delegation within a strategic-tactical hierarchy, offering an alternative to linear autonomy-progression models and informing AI tools that support rather than supplant human strategic control.
palavras_chave: Human-AI collaboration; collaborative design; domestication; bounded delegation; decision authority

titulo: Reflexive Qualitative Research and Generative AI: A Call to go Beyond the Binary
autores: Greenhalgh, T
resumo: Recent debates on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in qualitative research have been framed in increasingly polarized terms, positioning researchers as uncritical adopters or principled refusers. Drawing on recent position statements and editorial guidance, this article argues that such binary framing is unhelpful. While endorsing core concerns about meaning-making, reflexivity, bias, and environmental harm, it suggests that these concerns do not justify categorical rejection of all AI use. Instead, the article proposes refocusing debate on epistemic authority, distinguishing AI-led analysis from human-led practices, and developing governance-oriented responses to ethical and environmental risks. Moving beyond moral binaries is essential to preserving reflexive qualitative inquiry.
palavras_chave: reflexive qualitative research; generative artificial intelligence; epistemic authority; methodological integrity; research governance

titulo: Desire without satisfaction: object a, symbolic authority, and human-AI interaction
autores: Hamamra, B
resumo: This article develops a Lacanian analysis of conversational AI systems built on large language models by conceptualizing them as symbolic apparatuses that sustain desire rather than as neutral informational tools. Drawing on Jacques Lacan's theory of object a, desire, transference, and the Big Other, the paper argues that conversational AI does not satisfy desire but structurally sustains it by translating desire into demand and responding without closure. Because large language models operate through the symbolic register while lacking subjectivity, they can occupy positions of authority, knowledge, and responsiveness traditionally associated with the Other, thereby intensifying repetition, attachment, and epistemic investment. The article further shows that affective responses such as anxiety and uncanniness emerge not only from AI failure but also from excessive symbolic proximity, when object a appears too directly. Situating these dynamics within the political economy of attention and engagement, the paper challenges dominant AI ethics frameworks centered on accuracy, transparency, and trust calibration. Instead, it proposes a critical shift toward examining how conversational AI reorganizes the symbolic conditions of desire, authority, and subjectivity. By foregrounding lack, limit, and symbolic distance, the article offers a theoretical framework for understanding why conversational AI is simultaneously compelling and destabilizing.
palavras_chave: Object a; Desire; Conversational artificial intelligence; Symbolic order; Transference; AI ethics

titulo: When LLM Meets Simplicial Complex: A Novel Graph Prompt Learning on Ethereum Transaction Networks
autores: Liu, YX; Chan, S; Chu, J; Zhang, YY; Chen, YZ
veiculo: 2025 IEEE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON DATA MINING, ICDM
resumo: Fraudulent activity on blockchain networks poses significant risks to the integrity and trust of decentralized finance ecosystems. The timely and accurate detection of fraud nodes such as phishing addresses within large-scale Ethereum transaction networks remains a major challenge due to their dynamic, sparse, and evolving structures. While methods like graph deep learning (e.g., graph neural networks) have been extensively explored, they are not inherently designed to capture higher-order interactions and textual information embedded within graph data. Motivated by the urgent need for advanced and robust fraud detection techniques, we introduce a novel graph prompting method named Large Language Model-Simplicial Complex (LLM-SC) based graph prompting framework that leverages LLM-based multi-agent collaboration system, LLM-based financial news prompt function, and simplicial neural networks to capture both the structural and contextual dimensions of blockchain activity. The empirical studies demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, and these results provide a new tool for blockchain analytics platforms and regulatory authorities, enabling earlier and more accurate identification of fraudulent behavior and ultimately supporting safer and more resilient digital financial systems. The code is available at https://github.com/yl3564/LLM-SC.
palavras_chave: Ethereum; Blockchain; Graph prompting; Large language models; Simplicial complex

titulo: From peer review to protocol review: The ethical legitimacy of machine-to-machine evaluation
autores: Zhang, XF; Li, H
resumo: As generative AI becomes embedded in academic publishing, questions of efficiency and accuracy also raise questions about the authority of scholarly evaluation. Through normative and institutional analysis and a prospective thought experiment, this article distinguishes peer review from protocol review. Peer review uses protocols to support substantive judgment by people who engage with the manuscript, own the reasons offered, and remain answerable for decisions. Protocol review makes formalized criteria, learned proxies, or machine-generated evaluations substantially sufficient for a recommendation while human endorsement becomes nominal. Actual workflows lie on a continuum, and the threshold depends on the functions delegated and the human capacity to justify and revise the central reasons. Machine-to-machine evaluation denotes a connected workflow in which AI evaluates content substantially generated by other AI systems and the assessments inform further automated evaluation or editorial recommendations. Drawing on consequentialist, epistemic, and institutional accounts, the article argues that even superior performance on defined tasks leaves questions of review authority and responsibility to be resolved. The same standards apply to human and AI-assisted review. Seven linked conditions specify legitimate hybrid review through direct engagement, ownership of reasons, confidential infrastructure, functional disclosure, separation of automated checks from substantive judgment, institutional auditability, and human review and appeal. These conditions allow validated AI assistance while preserving accountable scholarly judgment.
palavras_chave: generative AI; peer review; protocol review; scientific self-governance; academic accountability

titulo: Lacanian Perspectives on Educational Futures in Human-AI Entanglement
autores: Creely, E
resumo: This conceptual investigation explores emergent possibilities for educational transformation through the evolving relationship between humans and generative artificial intelligence, theorised within Jacques Lacan's psychoanalytic framework. Rather than viewing AI as merely a technological tool, this analysis examines how human-AI entanglements open pedagogical territories that may reconstitute educational subjectivity and learning relationships. Drawing upon four Lacanian concepts, the symbolic order, objet petit a, jouissance, and the Real, this investigation maps educational possibilities emerging from posthuman subjectification processes. The symbolic order of traditional pedagogy, maintained through institutional authority and knowledge transmission, encounters productive disruption as AI systems generate discourse destabilising boundaries between teacher, student, and machine. Generative AI emerges as a novel form of objet petit a, functioning as an object of pedagogical desire promising complete knowledge whilst opening infinite possibilities through algorithmic unknowability. Educational jouissance may manifest as excessive enjoyment of AI-mediated learning, revealing libidinal investments in technological pedagogy exceeding instrumental need. The Real resurfaces through AI's capacity to generate content resisting conventional pedagogical integration, creating learning encounters that expose and expand meaning-making possibilities. This framework suggests human-AI educational hybridisation could catalyse emergent learning forms challenging humanist assumptions about knowledge authority and educational authenticity. In doing so, the article contributes to possibility studies by showing how Lacanian concepts help explain why some educational futures become imaginable whilst others remain foreclosed.
palavras_chave: generative AI; Lacan; education; pedagogy; posthuman

titulo: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Prevention of Intimate Partner Violence and Sexual Violence: A Scoping Review of the Literature
autores: Marcantonio, TL; Vowels, LM; LeRoux, S; Bravo, M; Thrash, A; Mueller, A; Niolet, A; Hall, M; Döring, N; Nadarzynski, T
resumo: Intimate partner and sexual violence (IPV/SV) remain pervasive global public health issues. Prevention efforts typically occur at the primary level (promoting consent and healthy relationships), secondary level (encouraging bystander intervention and screening), or tertiary level (supporting survivors through reporting and access to resources). The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots, including large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, presents new opportunities to expand access to information and potentially strengthen prevention efforts across these levels. However, little is known about how these tools are currently being used or evaluated within IPV/SV prevention. This scoping review synthesized 40 peer-reviewed articles, preprints, and conference papers published between 2017 and 2025 that examined AI chatbots in IPV/SV contexts. Twenty-six studies described the development of domain-specific chatbots designed to support survivors by documenting incidents of violence, facilitating or streamlining reporting to authorities, and connecting users with services such as counseling. In addition, general-purpose LLMS (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) appeared to consistently produced evidence-based and accurate responses to questions related to IPV/SV. Findings suggest that AI chatbots may have a meaningful role in IPV/SV prevention; however, most existing applications focus on tertiary prevention after harm has occurred. This emphasis mirrors broader policy and service landscapes that prioritize crisis response over primary prevention. To realize the potential of AI in this field, future researchers should explore how chatbots and LLMs can be incorporated into primary and secondary prevention, particularly in strengthening education, promoting healthy relationships, and supporting early intervention.

titulo: When Visibility Outpaces Expertise: Preserving Trustworthy Medical Authority in the Age of AI and Digital Amplification
autores: Ruiz-Bailén, M; Ruiz-Iniesta, MD
veiculo: JOURNAL OF EVALUATION IN CLINICAL PRACTICE
resumo: Contemporary medicine has unprecedented capacity to generate and disseminate information through social media, digital platforms and artificial intelligence. Visibility, communicative fluency and engagement-driven amplification may increasingly influence perceived credibility, contributing to an authority-expertise gap. This gap is not new: prestige, public prominence and institutional status have long functioned as imperfect proxies for competence. What is distinctive about generative AI is that it can relocate authority from identifiable people and institutions to interface-mediated outputs: answers are produced at scale, synthesised across sources, personalised to users and presented with fluency even when provenance and accountability are difficult to inspect. We therefore argue that AI changes the architecture rather than the existence of the problem. Drawing on virtue ethics, epistemology, critical care medicine and contemporary literature on digital communication, we propose that trustworthy medical authority requires alignment among epistemic validity, clinical wisdom and moral integrity. Social visibility remains an amplifier rather than a source of authority. Preserving trust in the AI era therefore requires not only accurate content but mechanisms that keep provenance, uncertainty and human accountability visible. Authority is not generated by fluency; it remains a professional and institutional achievement.
palavras_chave: clinical wisdom; digital communication; epistemology; generative artificial intelligence; medical authority; medical professionalism; professional trust; social media

titulo: Leveraging LLMs for Smart Cities Qualitative Data Analysis
autores: Covato, E; Soomro, K; Khan, Z; Bilal, M; Cormack, R; Green, S
resumo: Public authorities frequently conduct surveys and analyze data from citizens, a process that is often labor-intensive when performed manually. This paper explores how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can assist in automating data analysis for public authorities. In this respect, we investigate the potential of large language models (LLMs) to perform sentiment analysis and summarization of unstructured data as smart services. Using data from the East Bristol livable neighborhood (EBLN) as a case study, we assess the accuracy and precision of these models and validate the results against ground truth data and expert evaluations. Our findings indicate that sentiment classification achieved over 90% accuracy. Additionally, incorporating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further enhances the results obtained. Comparative analysis revealed that LLMs achieved superior performance over traditional summarization techniques based on domain expert evaluation. These results suggest that LLMs offer a promising and impactful approach to improving the efficiency of qualitative analysis, though further research is required to enhance their accuracy and usefulness.
palavras_chave: large language models; retrieval-augmented generation; sentiment analysis; smart cities; text summarization

titulo: Artificial intelligence-based data extraction for next generation risk assessment: Is fine-tuning of a large language model worth the effort?
autores: Sonnenburg, A; van der Lugt, B; Rehn, J; Wittkowski, P; Bech, K; Padberg, F; Eleftheriadou, D; Dobrikov, T; Bouwmeester, H; Mereu, C; Graf, F; Kneuer, C; Kramer, NI; Blümmel, T
resumo: To underpin scientific evaluations of chemical risks, agencies such as the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) heavily rely on the outcome of systematic reviews, which currently require extensive manual effort. One specific challenge constitutes the meaningful use of vast amounts of valuable data from new approach methodologies (NAMs) which are mostly reported in an unstructured way in the scientific literature. In the EFSA-initiated project 'AI4NAMS', the potential of large language models (LLMs) was explored. Models from the GPT family, where GPT refers to Generative Pre-trained Transformer, were used for searching, extracting, and integrating data from scientific publications for NAM-based risk assessment. A case study on bisphenol A (BPA), a substance of very high concern due to its adverse effects on human health, focused on the structured extraction of information on test systems measuring biologic activities of BPA. Fine-tuning of a GPT-3 model (Curie base model) for extraction tasks was tested and the performance of the fine-tuned model was compared to the performance of a ready-to-use model (text-davinci-002). To update findings from the AI4NAMS project and to check for technical progress, the fine-tuning exercise was repeated and a newer ready-to-use model (text-davinci-003) served as comparison. In both cases, the fine-tuned Curie model was found to be superior to the ready-to-use model. Performance improvement was also obvious between text-davinci-002 and the newer text-davinci-003. Our findings demonstrate how fine-tuning and the swift general technical development improve model performance and contribute to the growing number of investigations on the use of AI in scientific and regulatory tasks.
palavras_chave: Artificial intelligence; Risk Assessment; Systematic literature review; Automated data extraction; Large Language models; Fine-tuning

titulo: The Algorithmic Mujtahid: Artificial Intelligence, Ijtihad, and the Question of Interpretive Authority in Contemporary Islamic Ethics
autores: Amin, Z
resumo: The rise of artificial intelligence, particularly large language models, poses a unique epistemic challenge to Islamic interpretive authority. This paper explores the notion of the "Algorithmic Mujtahid," an AI system capable of engaging with foundational texts in ways resembling legal reasoning. We argue that AI forces a reconsideration of core concepts such as qasd, taqw & amacr;, and hikmah. By contrasting classical ijtihad's spiritual, teleological reasoning with machine learning's statistical logic, the study reveals both promise and limitation. Case studies in finance and bioethics show risks to scholarly hierarchy, concluding that AI must remain a subordinate, assistive tool rather than a replacement.
palavras_chave: Artificial intelligence; Islamic ethics; ijtih & amacr; d; interpretive authority; Maq & amacr; sid al-Shari'ah

titulo: A multilayered analysis of university students' experiences with human and AI-based feedback: A comparative examination of BERTopic, LLM models, and mixture of agents approaches
autores: Durak, HY; Onan, A
resumo: This study presents a multilayered text analysis framework for examining university students' experiences with human-and artificial intelligence (AI)-based feedback. The empirical corpus consisted of 322 feedback-related reflection statements obtained from 110 undergraduate students. The analysis combined data preprocessing, corpus-driven thematic modeling with BER-Topic, zero-shot thematic extraction using large language models (LLMs), ensemble-based semantic alignment, psycholinguistic emotion-theme integration, and high-resolution thematic refinement through a Mixture of Agents (MoA) framework. BERTopic identified six core themes: trust and transparency, cognitive load and clarity, learning contribution and perceived benefit, emotional discomfort and uncertainty, human-AI comparison, and complementary feedback expectations. The results showed that students' feedback experiences were multidimensional, involving cognitive, affective, explanatory, and comparative dimensions rather than a simple preference for either feedback source. BERTopic provided a stable corpus-grounded thematic baseline, whereas Large Language Model (LLM)-based zero-shot extraction produced pedagogically interpretable and conceptually expressive theme labels. The ensemble approach reduced variation across individual LLM outputs by consolidating semantically similar labels. MoA further refined thematic distinctions and improved emotion-topic alignment, particularly in statements involving cognitive ambiguity or emotionally charged feedback experiences. Comparative analyses indicated that AI-based feedback was more strongly associated with speed, accessibility, consistency, and immediate learning support, whereas human feedback was more strongly associated with contextual richness, empathy, pedagogical explanation, and perceived authority. The findings suggest that effective feedback design should combine the scalability and immediacy of AI-based feedback with human oversight, contextual interpretation, emotional calibration, and transparent justification. Overall, the study contributes to learning analytics and feedback research by demonstrating how corpus-driven topic modeling, LLM-based interpretation, ensemble alignment, and MoA-based refinement can be integrated to model the cognitive and affective dimensions of students' feedback experiences.
palavras_chave: Student experience; AI-based feedback; Human feedback; Topic modeling; BERTopic; Large Language Models; Mixture of Agents

titulo: Product Service System Innovation for Aging Societies: A Generative AI-Powered Human-AI Collaborative Design Framework
autores: Wang, YM; Wang, JY
resumo: To address the challenges of an aging society, this study proposes a generative AI-driven human-AI collaborative design framework to facilitate in novation in age-friendly Product-Service Systems (PSS). This framework trans cends conventional tool-based AI-assisted design paradigms by structurally guiding designers and AI in deep collaboration across critical phases including bigdata-driven needs insight, service system blueprint construction, touchpoint pro-totype design, and service scenario scripting. Specifically, AI leverages massivedata mining to expand insight dimensions into older adults' physiological, psy-chological, and social needs, while designers maintain authority over needs pri-oritization and ethical governance. Through human-AI collaboration, service system logic diagrams are generated, with AI rapidly producing multiple prototypeiterations that designers refine based on age-appropriate user experience princi-ples. This approach accelerates concept-to-prototype transformation while fostering more inclusive system solutions. The research emphasizes that collaborative innovation requires designers to possess critical thinking capabilities to harness AI's generative potential while mitigating inherent biases, achievable through training models on localized elderly user datasets and correcting solution deviations via interdisciplinary review. Future work will validate framework effectiveness through real-world age-friendly project pilots, ensuring designs align with the diverse and profound needs of Chinese older adults, thereby providing theoretical and methodological support for human-AI collaborative design practice in aging societies.
palavras_chave: Human-AI Collaboration; Age-Friendly Design; Product-Service Systems (PSS); Generative AI; Aging Society

titulo: Machine Learning and Large Language Model Decision Support for Medication-Error Prevention Across the Medication-Use Process: A Systematic Review with Implications for Saudi Arabia
autores: Alsaleh, EA; Alnemer, MJ; Alhassan, YHA; Khalil, AAA; Kaddoura, MA; Ishaqui, AA; Maqsood, MB; Iqbal, A
resumo: Objectives: Medication errors are a major source of preventable harm. We systematically reviewed workflow integrated artificial intelligence (AI) decision support (machine learning [ML], natural language processing, computer vision, and large language models [LLMs]) aimed at detecting, intercepting, or preventing medication errors, and considered implications for Saudi Arabia. Methods: We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, IEEE Xplore, and the Cochrane Library for English language studies published from January 2010 to February 2026. Eligible studies used real clinical/pharmacy data and evaluated an AI component designed to prevent or detect medication errors across prescribing/order verification, dispensing, administration, reconciliation, or medication directions. Two reviewers screened and extracted data independently; risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST, QUADAS2, or ROBINS-I. Results: A total of 16 studies met inclusion criteria. Nine evaluated prescribing/order verification tools (including look alike/sound alike and outlier detection), 3 evaluated administration support (including computer vision verification), 2 evaluated reconciliation/triage, 1 evaluated dispensing verification, and 1 evaluated an LLM for medication directions. Performance was often high for constrained tasks, but external validation, calibration, and explicit alert threshold governance were uncommon. Deployed evaluations suggested potential reductions in errors or near misses, but most impact evidence was observational, and alert burden/overrides were inconsistently reported. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; using GRADE, certainty of evidence for error reduction was generally low. Conclusion: Workflow integrated AI decision support can augment medication safety, particularly via high plus pressure variation surveillance and task specific verification, but the current evidence base provides limited causal certainty for harm reduction. For Saudi Arabia, scale up should be phased and governed through interoperability, clinical decision support governance, human factors evaluation, Saudi Food and Drug Authority aligned software as a medical device pathway, and post deployment monitoring.
palavras_chave: Artificial intelligence; Medication errors; Clinical decision support; Computer vision; Medication reconciliation; Large language models

titulo: From Algorithmic Scaffolding to Embodied Authority: Negotiating Human Expertise in AI-Mediated Fitness Coaching
autores: Liao, WY; Liu, N
veiculo: EXTENDED ABSTRACTS OF THE 2026 CHI CONFERENCE ON HUMAN FACTORS IN COMPUTING SYSTEMS, CHI 2026
resumo: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into professional work, yet its impact is often framed through task substitution and automation. Drawing on interviews, multi-sited observation, and professional immersion with fitness coaches, this poster examines how GenAI is incorporated into embodied service labor in practice. We find that trainers use GenAI as algorithmic scaffolding-delegating codified tasks such as program drafting and nutritional calculation-while retaining authority through embodied judgment, relational interaction, and real-time adaptation. When AI-generated plans encounter living bodies, standardized prescriptions frequently break down, revealing limits tied to bodily sensation, affect, and situational context. Rather than rejecting AI, practitioners actively negotiate these boundaries, repositioning their expertise around embodied articulation and client-facing work. These findings suggest that AI does not replace professional labor, but reorganizes where authority resides-standardizing baseline competence while amplifying the importance of embodied expertise. The study contributes early empirical insight into how embodiment shapes the limits of AI-mediated codification and human-AI collaboration in professional work.
palavras_chave: Generative AI; Progressive encapsulation; Embodied expertise; Human-AI collaboration; Professional authority

titulo: FINTEMPORAL: Complementing Large Language Models with Entity-Temporal Knowledge Graphs to Improve Numerical Accuracy in Financial Analysis
autores: Singh, S; Wang, C
veiculo: INTELLIGENT SYSTEMS AND APPLICATIONS, INTELLISYS 2026, VOL 3
resumo: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong linguistic capability but remain unreliable in numerical reasoning, limiting their use in financial analysis, where precision and traceability are essential. This study introduces FINTEMPORAL, a retrieval-augmented framework that integrates an entitytemporal knowledge graph with semantic embedding-based retrieval to improve numerical consistency in financial question answering. Using 15 years of structured monetary statistics from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, the system constructs a graph that explicitly models financial entities, hierarchical time components, and associated numerical values. Queries undergo entity and temporal extraction, followed by graph-guided retrieval and verification-supported LLM generation. Across 88 benchmark queries, FINTEMPORAL achieves 70.5% excellent numerical accuracy, outperforming GPT-4 (52.3%) and LLaMa-3 (48.9%), with significant gains in temporal comparisons and multi-entity reasoning. Statistical testing confirms that these improvements are unlikely to occur by chance. The findings demonstrate that structured knowledge representations, when coupled with LLMs, offer a practical and explainable path toward reliable numerical analysis in regulated financial domains.
palavras_chave: Large language models; Financial analysis; Knowledge graphs; Retrieval-augmented generation; Numerical reasoning; Temporal knowledge representation

titulo: Moral stereotyping in large language models
autores: Zewail, A; Figueroa, A; Graham, J; Atari, M
veiculo: PROCEEDINGS OF THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
resumo: Can Large Language Models (LLMs) accurately estimate various societies' moral values? Here, we query the perceptions of LLMs regarding the moral norms of the "average" person from 48 nations and compare them to a large-scale (n = 90,802) survey of six moral values (Care, Equality, Proportionality, Loyalty, Authority, and Purity) from those populations. Our findings indicate that LLMs poorly capture the moral diversity around the globe, systematically overestimating some moral values (particularly Care) and underestimating others (especially Purity). Notably, examining various versions of Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) shows that these LLMs may overestimate the overall moral concerns of some Western countries (e.g., the United States, Canada, and Australia) while underestimating those of non-Western countries (e.g., Nigeria, Morocco, and Indonesia). Our work demonstrates that LLMs are inaccurate generators of cross-cultural estimations in the moral domain; in other words, they stereotype the moral values of non-Western populations in predictable ways. Our results highlight the ethical and epistemic risks of relying on LLMs to estimate the endorsement of moral values around the globe.
palavras_chave: morality; large language models; culture; AI

titulo: Mapping Moral Reasoning Circuits: A Mechanistic Analysis of Ethical Decision-Making in Large Language Models
autores: Schacht, S; Lanquillon, C
veiculo: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HCI, AI-HCI 2025, PT II
resumo: This paper systematically investigates how large language models (LLMs) encode moral reasoning across six moral dimensions: care, fairness, loyalty, authority, sanctity, and liberty. We propose a novel interpretability pipeline that combines differential activation analysis, automated neuron description, and ablation experiments to identify specialized neurons aligned with each moral dimension. Our curated dataset of 240 validated moral and immoral statement pairs guides this exploration and reveals that certain neurons consistently exhibit increased activation in response to morally aligned statements. Notably, the care and sanctity dimensions show the largest sets of specialized neurons, whereas fairness and loyalty show fewer. We further demonstrate that ablating these neurons can causally modulate ethical decision-making, supporting the presence of discrete sub-circuits that influence moral outputs. Our findings not only advance the theoretical understanding of moral reasoning in LLMs, but also highlight avenues for targeted interventions and alignment. (All materials from this paper, including code, data, and experimental results, are available at https://github.com/coairesearch/mapping_moral_reasoning.git.)
palavras_chave: Mechanistic Interpretability; Large Language Models; Moral Reasoning; Moral Foundation Theory

titulo: "ItWould Take Too Much to Explain": Task-Contingent AI Use in Design Education
autores: Dines, N; Mokryn, O
veiculo: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 8TH EDUCHI SYMPOSIUM ON HCI EDUCATION, EDUCHI 2026
resumo: Self-regulated learning research emphasizes strategic tool selection as central to effective learning. Generative AI complicates this process by offering broad capabilities whose value depends on task context. While concerns have been raised about shifts in authority and reduced learner agency, there is limited empirical evidence of how students decide when to use or decline AI across different tasks. We report a naturalistic study of 23 students in a semester-long design course who worked with custom LLM agents across four sequential tasks. Aside from one explicit boundary prohibiting AI use for stakeholder interviews, students retained autonomy over tool use. AI engagement varied systematically. Students sought validation during interview design, largely declined AI when documenting how interviews reshaped system logic, showed mixed use during envisioning exercises, and selectively delegated during final solution development. These patterns suggest task-contingent judgment rather than uniform reliance or resistance. We argue that making such judgment explicit is an important learning goal in AI-mediated education.
palavras_chave: self-regulated learning; epistemic agency; generative AI; metacognition; task-technology fit; design education; human-AI interaction

titulo: When machines explain medicine: Nursing ethics and clinical communication
autores: Yang, XW; Liang, YW; Liu, YJ; Liu, D; Yang, L; Zhang, B; Xu, C; Wu, YH; He, JY
resumo: Clinical communication is ethically consequential, shaping how diagnostic information is interpreted, trusted, and acted upon. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to reformulate technical reports into patient-facing explanations. Although such 'plain-language' outputs can improve comprehension and reduce communication workload, their ethical implications for everyday clinical communication, particularly in nursing practice, remain underexamined. This article provides a normative ethical analysis of how LLM-mediated explanations reshape clinical communication. It addresses three interrelated questions: how automated explanation redistributes interpretive authority among clinicians, nurses, patients, and algorithmic systems; how this redistribution affects responsibility and accountability; and how LLM-mediated explanations influence the ethical communication of uncertainty and trust in routine care. The analysis is informed by peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2022 and 2025 on LLM-assisted explanation in radiology and pathology communication, identified through a focused, non-systematic search of major biomedical databases. Drawing on this literature, the article examines how automated explanation reshapes clinical meaning-making in contexts characterised by informational complexity and diagnostic uncertainty. Across existing studies, a consistent pattern emerges: as explanation becomes partially automated and more widely accessible, interpretive framing increasingly occurs outside clinician-patient dialogue, including through workflow-integrated tools and patient-side consultation. Interpretive authority is thus distributed across clinicians, nurses, patients, and platform-based systems, while formal accountability remains concentrated within professional roles. We argue that LLM-assisted explanation should be understood as mediation rather than neutral translation, raising important ethical questions about interpretive authority, responsibility, and the representation of uncertainty in clinical communication.
palavras_chave: large language models; clinical communication; nursing ethics; interpretive authority; accountability; uncertainty communication

titulo: Unpacking how humanities and social sciences undergraduate students maintain agency in GenAI-assisted learning
autores: Ge, ZG; Li, Q
resumo: The integration of Generative AI (GenAI) into higher education raises critical questions about how students maintain intellectual agency while engaging with generative systems, particularly in the humanities and social sciences (HSS), where interpretation, argumentation, and authorship are central. Addressing this issue, this study employs a grounded theory approach to examine how HSS undergraduate students sustain agency in GenAI-assisted learning. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 37 students across multiple disciplines, and data were analyzed using open, axial, and selective coding. Based on this analysis, the study develops the Strategic Engagement and Critical Evaluation model, which conceptualizes agency as an ongoing regulatory process enacted through critical assessment of AI outputs, boundary setting, and adaptive prompting. The findings indicate that students operate as "humans in the loop," continuously calibrating trust while retaining evaluative authority over AI-generated content. By offering a process-oriented explanation of agency in human-AI interaction, the study also identifies implications for explainable AI design and educational policy.
palavras_chave: Human-AI interaction; generative AI; humanities and social sciences; agency; grounded theory

titulo: 'Chattable' Avatars: Using LLMs to Power Visitor Engagement with Historical Persons
autores: Jiang, ZL; Qin, YP; Finnegan, DJ
veiculo: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 38TH INTERNATIONAL BCS HUMAN-COMPUTER INTERACTION CONFERENCE, BCS HCI 2025
resumo: Cultural Heritage institutions such as Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums are tasked with preservingour history and heritage for future generations while engaging new audiences with an appetite for said engagement to be increasingly digital and interactive. To explore how advances in natural language processing, particularly large languagemodels (LLMs), may help GLAMs in their mission, we designed a prototype 'Chattable' avatar, a 3D high-polygon animated character which visitors can talk to and interact with. We report the design of our avatar, and a workshop we conducted with curators and staff from a GLAM institution, to understand the problems, requirements, and opportunities LLMs present in the cultural heritage space. We present results froma qualitative analysis of our workshop highlighting themes such as trust, authority, social experience, and location, finding LLMs may be more suited to deployments focused on non-factual data dissemination. We conclude with implications for GLAMs and suggestions for future research to realise how best to integrate Generative AI like LLMs into the GLAM space.
palavras_chave: Generative AI; Museums and Galleries; Qualitative Research; LLMs; Workshop

titulo: 'This here is a true representation of who I was': Synthetic media and the authority of the dead
autores: Meikle, G; Sumiala, J
resumo: The dead are increasingly being resurrected through synthetic media. This article draws inspiration from the histories of both manipulated media and mediations of death to examine two contemporary cases in which synthetic representations of dead individuals are deployed in attempts to influence issues of gun violence. The article asks in what ways and to what ends these deceased victims are being exploited. The analytical approach uses qualitative textual analysis. The authors find that these dead are imputed a form of agency within communicative networks and identify communicative strategies of encouraging suspension of disbelief and of invoking deictic references to the here and now in order to leverage the authority of the dead. The article concludes that such exploitation of the authority of the dead raises questions around the rights and responsibilities of publics, of digital platforms, and of the dead themselves.
palavras_chave: death; synthetic media; digital resurrection; generative AI; manipulated media; deepfakes

titulo: A Framework for Generative AI-Driven Assessment in Higher Education
autores: Ilieva, G; Yankova, T; Ruseva, M; Kabaivanov, S
resumo: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into educational environments raises both opportunities and concerns regarding assessment design, academic integrity, and quality assurance. While new generation AI tools offer new modes of interactivity, feedback, and content generation, their use in assessment remains insufficiently pedagogically framed and regulated. In this study, we propose a new framework for generative AI-supported assessment in higher education, structured around the needs and responsibilities of three key stakeholders (branches): instructors, students, and control authorities. The framework outlines how teaching staff can design adaptive and AI-informed tasks and provide feedback, how learners can engage with these tools transparently, and how institutional bodies can ensure accountability through compliance standards, policies, and audits. This three-branch multi-level model contributes to the emerging discourse on responsible AI adoption in higher education by offering a holistic approach for integrating AI-based systems into assessment practices while safeguarding academic values and quality.
palavras_chave: generative artificial intelligence; higher education; digital pedagogy; educational technology; assessment; AI-supported assessment; framework for assessment; academic integrity; responsible AI use

titulo: Generative AI, algorithmic subjectivation and the conditions of thought
autores: Hamamra, B
resumo: Contemporary accounts of generative artificial intelligence frame it as an instrument managed through ethics, governance, or responsible use. I argue that this framing leaves its philosophical stakes underexamined because it retains a conception of cognition external to technical mediation. Drawing on Gilbert Simondon's theory of individuation, I examine generative AI through its reorganization of the technical conditions of thought. This claim does not grant subjectivity to language models. It identifies the technical milieu in which subjects recognize thought as adequate and shareable. I use algorithmic subjectivation for the formation of subject positions, habits of attention, and standards of adequacy through algorithmic mediation. I introduce probabilistic reason for the institutional authority acquired by generated coherence without interpretation or accountable judgment. I introduce synthetic transindividuation for the technical production of collective semblance within human transindividual relations when generated discourse circulates without shared experience, responsibility, or reciprocal becoming. I develop technical care from Stiegler's pharmacology of technics as a structural practice that sustains individuation, responsibility, and subject formation within technical mediation.
palavras_chave: Individuation; Probabilistic reason; Synthetic transindividuation; Generative artificial intelligence; Technical care

titulo: Retrieval Augmented Generation-Based Large Language Models for Bridging Transportation Cybersecurity Legal Knowledge Gaps
autores: Akbar, KA; Uddin, MN; Khan, L; Hockstad, T; Rahman, M; Chowdhury, M; Thuraisingham, B
resumo: With the advancement of connected and automated transportation systems, a growing need has emerged for regulatory authorities to update existing laws and statutes, as well as create new ones, to address future implications of connectivity and automation. Specifically, ensuring proper engagement with cybersecurity and data privacy challenges for connected and automated transportation systems will require a comprehensive legal framework at both the federal and state levels. To help policymakers achieve this, a retrieval augmented generation (RAG)-based large language model (LLM) framework, Transportation Cybersecurity and Resiliency (TraCR) AI, has been developed in this study, focusing on extracting pertinent information from existing legislation based on inquiries and crafting LLM-generated responses to highlight potential loopholes for further scrutiny. This study primarily aims to mitigate the hallucinations caused in the domain of LLMs by developing a curated knowledge base of legislative documents and an associated question-answer dataset to improve the effectiveness of query results. This RAG-based framework extracts relevant information to improve the specificity of answers and aids the LLM in providing factually accurate responses with increased reliability. Our analyses reveal that the presented RAG-based framework can aid legislative analysis by generating queries for particular questions and responses. We also compare our RAG framework-generated responses with commercially available LLMs to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. TraCR AI outperforms leading commercial LLMs across four distinct metrics, that is, AlignScore, ParaScore, BERTScore, and ROUGE score. This highlights that integrating RAG allows LLMs to produce more factually accurate and up-to-date responses than standalone LLMs. This approach to domain-specific LLM development will improve the quality of legislative analysis that can be used to aid policymakers in meeting the challenge of updating legal codes in accordance with emerging technologies.
palavras_chave: large language model; hallucination; cybersecurity; transportation; policy; legal

titulo: Governing generative AI under uncertainty: institutional anchoring and regime formation in urban school districts
autores: Wu, E; Rodriguez, L
resumo: This paper examines how large urban school districts in the United States govern generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in the absence of comprehensive federal or state regulatory mandates. Drawing on a comparative analysis of twenty-nine governance artifacts produced between 2023 and early 2026 across four major districts (Chicago Public Schools, New York City Public Schools, the School District of Philadelphia, and Miami-Dade County Public Schools), the study identifies four distinct AI governance regimes anchored in different institutional logics. Chicago constructs an infrastructure-embedded regime that integrates AI governance into administrative modernization and compliance systems. New York anchors authority in statutory transparency mandates and algorithmic reporting requirements. Philadelphia governs through professional mediation and bounded vendor authorization. Miami represents a formation-stage regime in which governance structures remain under deliberative construction. The study advances a policy-centered argument: under conditions of regulatory uncertainty, districts do not merely adopt or restrict AI; they construct provisional governance regimes that stabilize the institutional meaning of AI in public education. These regimes reflect distinct theories of control, accountability, and institutional responsibility. Their differences carry equity implications, distributing risk and authority unevenly across educators, students, and vendors. The findings contribute to educational policy scholarship by theorizing district-level AI governance as institutional anchoring under uncertainty and demonstrating how early local decisions may entrench or mitigate disparities before higher-level regulatory frameworks solidify.
palavras_chave: Generative AI governance; School districts; institutional anchoring; educational policy; sociotechnical governance; K-12 education

titulo: ChatGPT in education: global reactions to AI innovations
autores: Futterer, T; Fischer, C; Alekseeva, A; Chen, XB; Tate, T; Warschauer, M; Gerjets, P
resumo: The release and rapid diffusion of ChatGPT have caught the attention of educators worldwide. Some educators are enthusiastic about its potential to support learning. Others are concerned about how it might circumvent learning opportunities or contribute to misinformation. To better understand reactions about ChatGPT concerning education, we analyzed Twitter data (16,830,997 tweets from 5,541,457 users). Based on topic modeling and sentiment analysis, we provide an overview of global perceptions and reactions to ChatGPT regarding education. ChatGPT triggered a massive response on Twitter, with education being the most tweeted content topic. Topics ranged from specific (e.g., cheating) to broad (e.g., opportunities), which were discussed with mixed sentiment. We traced that authority decisions may influence public opinions. We discussed that the average reaction on Twitter (e.g., using ChatGPT to cheat in exams) differs from discussions in which education and teaching-learning researchers are likely to be more interested (e.g., ChatGPT as an intelligent learning partner). This study provides insights into people's reactions when new groundbreaking technology is released and implications for scientific and policy communication in rapidly changing circumstances.

titulo: Navigating the integration of ChatGPT in UAE's government sector: challenges and opportunities
autores: Goher, GN
resumo: PurposeThis research examines how responsible deployment of ChatGPT in the UAE's government sector, guided by New Public Management principles, can enhance customer journeys by integrating services across government bodies. Through semi-structured interviews with UAE government officers, the study investigates this approach's benefits, challenges, and applications for achieving efficient and integrated public service delivery.Design/methodology/approachThis research adopts a qualitative approach, purposive sampling strategy, and semi-structured interviews to explore the subjective viewpoints of 20 high-level UAE government authorities. The thematic analysis uncovers ChatGPT's benefits, challenges, and applications, aligning with New Public Management principles.FindingsThematic analysis reveals four themes: Benefits and Applications of ChatGPT, Challenges, Strategies to Overcome Challenges, and Steps for Customer Journey Enhancement through ChatGPT.Research limitations/implicationsThe analysis is based on participant responses provided during the interviews, which may be subject to biases or incomplete information. Secondly, the study focuses solely on the provided applications and participant responses, limiting the generalizability of the conclusions to other contexts.Practical implicationsThe implementation of ChatGPT in the government sector has practical implications for transforming its operations and enhancing communication, efficiency, decision-making, and service offerings: citizen engagement, streamlined processes, and informed governance.Originality/valueThis study uniquely examines ChatGPT's role in government, offering insights into communication, efficiency, decision-making, and service offerings. Identifying hurdles enriches understanding of ChatGPT's practical integration in government.
palavras_chave: ChatGPT; Government sector; Public service delivery; Benefits of ChatGPT; Applications of ChatGPT; Limitations of ChatGPT; New public management

titulo: Trustworthy Digital Auxiliary Processes for Sustainable Energy Utilization: A Targeted Process-Oriented Review and Conceptual Evidence-to-Review Framework
autores: Moon, J
resumo: Sustainable energy systems increasingly rely on digital auxiliary processes that convert telemetry, forecasts, diagnostic evidence, and operating rules into reviewable information for authorized human decision-makers. This targeted review develops a transparent and traceable conceptual evidence-to-review framework for photovoltaic, wind, storage, fuel-cell, and converter-coupled systems. The coded review pool comprised 100 sources, including 75 analytical and 25 contextual sources; 10 additional references supported methodological, technical, and case-specific context and were not included in thematic coding. A six-stage thematic analysis, supported by a revision-stage coding audit, identified five analytical layers: data-quality control, forecasting and uncertainty, explanation diagnostics, constrained evidence briefing, and accountable human review. These layers were translated into an eight-stage advisory architecture that separates evidence preparation, validation, briefing, and review from the authorized control plane. No direct large-language-model-to-controller or model-to-asset path is permitted. An illustrative Jeju scenario traces one evidence record through the architecture and shows how safety conditions, evidence admissibility, and procedural authority lead to CHECK, HOLD, or ESCALATE outcomes. The review concludes that trustworthy digital support requires traceable evidence, deterministic safety and rule boundaries, and accountable human authorization.
palavras_chave: sustainable energy utilization; evidence-to-review framework; data quality; uncertainty quantification; explainable artificial intelligence; retrieval-augmented generation; large language models; converter-coupled systems; accountable human review

titulo: Feeling seen by something that doesn't feel: simulated empathy, epistemic vigilance, and ethics of AI
autores: Bartell, SM
resumo: This essay examines simulated empathy in generative AI, arguing that rhetorical fluency can create the illusion of recognition without reciprocity. It frames AI empathy as a linguistic performance that mimics care while lacking cognition, accountability, and moral relation. The essay warns that mistaking fluency for understanding can weaken critique, flatten judgment, and displace human relationships. It calls for epistemic vigilance in AI-mediated feedback and offers a vocabulary for understanding how simulated empathy shapes trust, authority, and responsibility in higher education.
palavras_chave: AI empathy; epistemic vigilance; rhetorical fluency; AI-mediated feedback; pedagogical ethics

titulo: Trusting Generative AI for Health Advice: Preregistered Survey Experiment
autores: Landrum, AR; Verma, N; Kehrberg, A
resumo: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly used for health information seeking, yet it remains unclear how the public evaluates AI-generated health advice relative to guidance from credentialed clinicians in digital environments. Understanding the conditions under which AI is perceived as credible is critical as these systems become integrated into digital health ecosystems. Objective: This study examined how source type (a human nurse in an online portal, a health care-specialized generative artificial intelligence system framed as an "AI nurse," or ChatGPT [OpenAI], a general-purpose chatbot), message characteristics, contextual risk, values framing, and individual differences in medical skepticism and experience with AI shape credibility evaluations of the provided advice and its purported source. Methods: In a preregistered online experiment, a national sample of US adult participants (N=1502) was randomly assigned to 1 of 3 source conditions and evaluated health advice across 3 scenarios: low risk (dietary advice for cholesterol), high risk (chest pain triage), and a morally sensitive scenario (egg freezing). Advice type (intuitive vs counterintuitive) was manipulated in the risk scenarios, and ideological framing (neutral, conservative-leaning, and liberal-leaning) was manipulated in the morally sensitive scenario. Primary outcomes included participants' perceived credibility of the advice and beliefs about whether the patient should follow it. Source-level perceptions of competence and benevolence were also assessed. Medical skepticism and prior AI experience were examined as moderators. Results: Advice attributed to a human nurse was rated as more credible than advice attributed to either AI source. Message intuitiveness showed effects comparable to, and sometimes larger than, the effects of source: intuitive advice was perceived as more credible than counterintuitive advice, with this difference amplified in high-risk contexts. In the morally sensitive scenario, ideological framing influenced perceived bias but did not interact significantly with source. Medical skepticism moderated source evaluations: higher skepticism was associated with greater perceived competence of the AI nurse and lower perceived competence of the human nurse. Conclusions: Generative AI is evaluated within existing credibility frameworks rather than dismissed outright as inferior to human expertise. While licensed clinicians retain a credibility advantage, AI-generated advice is generally perceived as competent and legitimate. Importantly, individuals skeptical of traditional medical authority may evaluate AI-based guidance more favorably, suggesting that AI systems may redistribute-rather than uniformly erode-trust in health advice. As AI tools become embedded in patient-facing health platforms, message design and audience characteristics may shape acceptance more strongly than source labeling alone.
palavras_chave: artificial intelligence; ChatGPT; digital health; health communication; health information seeking; medical skepticism; risk perception; trust

titulo: Information extraction framework for spanish notarized documents using end-to-end data
autores: Villa-García, PA; Alonso-Calvo, R; García-Remesal, M
resumo: Notarized documents serve as certified records of acts and contracts overseen by notaries, conferring unchallengeable legal authority. These documents significantly reduce transaction costs in goods and services markets, with millions produced and utilized annually by stakeholders, including banks, insurance companies, and government agencies. Extracting information from these unstructured documents is essential for automating business processes reliant on their content. However, this task is challenging due to the distinct characteristics of these legal documents and the limited availability of datasets and language models in Spanish. This paper addresses the issue of Information Extraction from Spanish notarized documents. We propose a framework that relies solely on end-to-end data usage, enabling the extraction of legal elements without labeled datasets. Our framework is effective in legal domains, particularly with notarized documents, where text extraction from scanned documents is common and often affected by optical character recognition noise. We created a new dataset from a corpus of notarized documents and fine-tuned several pretrained multilingual language models, including mT5, mBART, and the large language model BLOOMZ. Additionally, we developed a model from scratch based on the T5 architecture, utilizing a corpus of Spanish notarized documents. The promising results, with an F1 score of 96.13, validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework compared to existing methods in legal document information extraction.
palavras_chave: Information extraction; End-to-end data; Notarized documents; Post-OCR correction; Pretrained language models; Large language models

titulo: Artificial Authority: The Promise and Perils of LLM Judges in Healthcare
autores: Genovese, A; Hegstrom, L; Prabha, S; Gomez-Cabello, CA; Haider, SA; Collaco, B; Wood, NG; Forte, AJ
resumo: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into clinical documentation, decision support, and patient-facing applications across healthcare, including plastic and reconstructive surgery. Yet, their evaluation remains bottlenecked by costly, time-consuming human review. This has given rise to LLM-as-a-judge, in which LLMs are used to evaluate the outputs of other AI systems. Methods: This review examines LLM-as-a-judge in healthcare with particular attention to judging architectures, validation strategies, and emerging applications. A narrative review of the literature was conducted, synthesizing LLM judge methodologies as well as judging paradigms, including those applied to clinical documentation, medical question-answering systems, and clinical conversation assessment. Results: Across tasks, LLM judges align most closely with clinicians on objective criteria (e.g., factuality, grammaticality, internal consistency), benefit from structured evaluation and chain-of-thought prompting, and can approach or exceed inter-clinician agreement, but remain limited for subjective or affective judgments and by dataset quality and task specificity. Conclusions: The literature indicates that LLM judges can enable efficient, standardized evaluation in controlled settings; however, their appropriate role remains supportive rather than substitutive, and their performance may not generalize to complex plastic surgery environments. Their safe use depends on rigorous human oversight and explicit governance structures.
palavras_chave: artificial intelligence; large language model; clinical decision support systems; decision making; computer assisted; benchmarking; LLM-as-a-judge

titulo: Toward justice-focused participatory research repositories: Connecting technical and professional communication, critical archive studies, and community-led AI practices
autores: Shivers-McNair, A
resumo: This review of research argues that TPC researchers engaging with communities in design work can build repositories of their design research materials as sites of collaboration and shared authority with the communities we engage. I bring together threads within TPC and from critical archival studies and community-led applications of generative AI, highlighting the possibilities and pitfalls for TPC researchers aiming to cultivate collaborative repositories of research that honor communities' insights and ownership of their data.
palavras_chave: Archives; community-led AI; participatory research; research repositories

titulo: Harmful Prompt Classification for Large Language Models
autores: Gupta, O; Lozano, MD; Busalim, A; Jaiswal, RR; Quille, K
veiculo: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 2024 CONFERENCE ON HUMAN CENTERED ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-EDUCATION AND PRACTICE, HCAI-EP 2024
resumo: Over the last few years, using LLM chatbots like ClaudeAI, Co-pilot and ChatGPT for text generation has become a regular habit for many, with over 100 million weekly users flocking to ChatGPT alone. One side effect of such vast usage of these models is undesirable prompts being submitted to the model. This not only risks data and model poisoning if done repeatedly but also causes harm to society through the responses provided by the models, which are then in turn trained on such models. It is the onus of the model creators and company to address these undesirable prompts based on the type of harm present. To this end, model developers have started conducting Red-teaming of LLMs, a form of evaluation that elicits model vulnerabilities potentially leading to such undesirable behaviours. There are existing classifiers that detect whether a prompt is harmful and censor the models' responses for safe user access. However, for developers, more metadata on the category of danger that a prompt presents equips them with a capability to prepare for such attacks on the model based on the frequency and type of harm. Additionally, in cases where further investigation is required, companies can report problematic user behaviour to the authorities. Hence the importance of categorising harmful prompts. We propose a sub-category based prompt classifier that identifies the specific type of harm that a damaging prompt is addressing to help content moderators and governance functions take further actions. Using explainable AI methods, we focused on both blackbox and white-box testing of models and explored Linear SVM, KNN and BERT for further sub-classifying harmful prompts, and obtained accuracies of 92%, 85% and 87% respectively.

titulo: When high-autonomy generative AI undermines "This is mine": Psychological ownership in consumer co-creation
autores: Wu, YX; Guo, ZW; Li, MH
veiculo: JOURNAL OF RETAILING AND CONSUMER SERVICES
resumo: As generative AI becomes embedded in consumer co-creation, firms increasingly allow AI systems not only to support design but also make substantive design decisions for consumers. This shift raises an important question: how does AI autonomy affect consumers' evaluations of co-created products? Drawing on psychological ownership theory, this research examines whether high AI autonomy reduces purchase intention by weakening consumers' felt ownership of the co-created output. Across four experiments using interactive product cocreation interfaces, we find consistent evidence for this explanation. Study 1 shows that high AI autonomy reduces an incentive-compatible behavioral purchase decision. Study 2 replicates the negative effect on purchase intention and shows that psychological ownership, rather than perceived quality, explains the effect. Study 3 identifies participation depth as a boundary condition: the negative effect of high AI autonomy is weaker when consumers participate more deeply in the co-creation process, and this attenuation operates through psychological ownership rather than perceived effort or perceived control. Study 4 identifies product self-expressiveness as a second boundary condition: the negative effect of high AI autonomy is stronger for more self-expressive products, again through psychological ownership rather than retailer innovativeness. The findings advance psychological ownership theory by showing how AI autonomy changes the visibility of consumer contribution in human-AI co-creation and offer practical guidance for designing AI-assisted co-creation interfaces that preserve visible consumer contribution, final decision authority, and felt ownership of the co-created output.
palavras_chave: Generative AI; AI autonomy; Consumer co-creation; Psychological ownership; Participation depth; Self-expressiveness; Purchase intention

titulo: Digital bias in sexuality education: an intersectional analysis of AI responses to simulated Italian adolescents
autores: Ederoclite, M; Tzankova, II; Villano, P
resumo: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by adolescents to seek information about sexuality, relationships, and well-being. However, little is known about how these systems discursively construct and mediate such interactions. This study examines how three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) respond to simulated Italian adolescent personas used as analytical probes for algorithmic bias. Drawing on 120 standardized Italian-language interactions across four personas differing by gender, class, ethnicity, and sexual orientation, the analysis investigates how identity markers shape the framing of sexual and affective health information. Qualitative analysis reveals recurrent patterns of medicalization, differential agency attribution, and cultural othering. As markers of marginalization accumulate, AI responses exhibit a systematic discursive shift from normalization toward surveillance framing and referral to professional authority. To account for this pattern, we introduce intersectional amplification as an analytical construct grounded in Italian-language interactions about adolescent sexuality with commercial LLMs, capturing a situated process of discursive differentiation within this sociotechnical configuration. Overall, the findings show that LLM-mediated sexuality education reproduces normative hierarchies embedded in training data, positioning adolescents differently along axes of privilege and marginality. Crucially, the study demonstrates that such inequalities are not imposed by technical constraints but reflect design priorities.
palavras_chave: Artificial intelligence; Sexual health education; Algorithmic bias; Intersectionality; Adolescence; Human-computer interaction

titulo: Revisiting Framing Codebooks with AI: Employing Large Language Models as Analytical Collaborators in Deductive Content Analysis
autores: Gómez-Zará, D; Valdivieso, H; Pérez, J; Parra, D; Valenzuela, S
resumo: Codebooks are central to framing research, providing theoretically grounded criteria for analyzing news content. While codebooks are traditionally built from theoretical frameworks and researchers' knowledge, applying them to large news corpora often exposes ambiguities, borderline cases, and underspecified rules that are difficult to resolve through theory alone. Moreover, news corpora evolve over time and differ across cultures, necessitating that researchers revisit the theoretical frameworks underlying these codebooks. In this article, we propose a workflow that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to augment the creation and refinement of framing codebooks by combining theoretical frameworks with data-driven exploration. Rather than treating LLMs as automated classifiers, this approach positions them as analytic collaborators that help externalize decision rules, surface latent dimensions, and support iterative revisions of codebooks through dialogues between researchers and their data. We illustrate this workflow using a dataset of Latin American news coverage, demonstrating how applying LLMs' capabilities has surfaced latent patterns, generated frame distinctions, and adapted frameworks to new contexts. This method provides an LLM-assisted strategy that supports methodological creativity while preserving researchers' interpretative authority.
palavras_chave: Large language models; artificial intelligence; deductive coding; Human-AI interaction; framing coding

titulo: AI's patriarchal grammar: How large language models distort feminist legal analysis
autores: Parmar, D; Desouza, S
resumo: This article argues that AI language models can produce what we term "patriarchal grammar:" a recurring distortion of feminist legal scholarship through the euphemization of sexual violence, the erasure of structural feminist critique, and the naturalization of patriarchal assumptions as neutral facts. These distortions pose a serious epistemic risk to feminist legal analysis, particularly in postcolonial Asian contexts where English mediates legal discourse. Using ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini on the 2022 Indian marital rape case (RIT Foundation v. Union of India), we observed that in the selected encounters documented here, these models transformed "marital rape" into "intimate disputes," reduced Justice Shakdher's feminist constitutional reasoning to generic rights discourse and presented Justice Hari Shankar's patriarchal logic as objective fact. These encounters are presented with sufficient contextual detail to enable critical evaluation, though full replicability is constrained by the instability of hosted commercial AI systems. Following Gayatri Spivak, we ask for whom we are making language accessible, and to what effect. While AI tools promise linguistic equity, they risk enacting epistemic violence by selectively filtering feminist analysis through dominant patriarchal frameworks. We conclude by proposing protocols for feminist scholars to preserve epistemological authority when engaging with AI tools.
palavras_chave: Artificial intelligence; feminist legal theory; marital rape; India; epistemic injustice; machine translation

titulo: Automating Cyber Risk Assessment With Public LLMs: An Expert-Validated Framework and Comparative Analysis
autores: Unal, NM; Celiktas, B
resumo: Traditional cyber risk assessment methodologies face a critical dilemma: they are either quantitative yet static and context-agnostic (e.g., CVSS), or context-aware yet highly labor-intensive and subjective (e.g., NIST SP 800-30). Consequently, organizations struggle to scale risk assessment to match the pace of evolving threats. This paper presents an automated, context-aware risk assessment framework that leverages the reasoning capabilities of publicly available Large Language Models (LLMs) to operationalize expert knowledge. Rather than positioning the LLM as the final decision-maker, the framework decouples semantic interpretation from risk scoring authority through a transparent, deterministic Dynamic Metric Engine. Unlike complex closed box machine learning models, our approach anchors the AI's reasoning to this expert-validated metric schema, with weights derived using the Rank Order Centroid (ROC) method from a survey of 101 cybersecurity professionals. We evaluated the framework through a comparative study involving 15 diverse real-world vulnerability scenarios (C-1-C-15) and three supplementary sensitivity stress tests (C-16-C-18 ). The validation scenarios were independently assessed by a cohort of ten senior human experts and two state-of-the-art LLM agents (GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash). The results show that the LLM-driven agents achieve scoring consistency closely aligned with the human median (Pearson r ranging from 0.9390 to 0.9717, Spearman rho from 0.8472 to 0.9276) against a highly reliable expert baseline (Cronbach's alpha=0.996 ), while reducing the assessment cycle time by more than 100 & times; (averaging under 4 seconds per case vs. a human average of 6 minutes). Furthermore, a dedicated context sensitivity analysis (C-13-C-15 ) indicates that the framework adapts risk scores based on organizational context (e.g., SME vs. Critical Infrastructure) for identical technical vulnerabilities. Importantly, the system is designed not merely to replicate expert intuition, but to enforce bounded, policy-consistent risk evaluation under predefined governance constraints. Overall, these findings suggest that commercially available LLMs, when constrained by expert-validated metric schemas, can support reproducible, transparent, and real-time risk assessments.
palavras_chave: Risk management; Measurement; Computer security; Engines; Cognition; Surveys; Cyber threat intelligence; Closed box; ISO Standards; Generative AI; Cyber risk assessment; large language models (LLMs); generative AI; rank order centroid (ROC); automated risk scoring; human-AI comparison
